candidates.text: For every deadline or date-based obligation, explicitly state whether the governing document includes Business Day adjustment provisions. If absent, flag the ambiguity and recommend clarifying language rather than assuming adjustments.

When analyzing date-based obligations, never assume Business Day adjustments apply unless explicitly stated in the document. Use a date calculator to verify the exact calendar date and document whether adjustments are required by the governing terms.

In timeline analyses, include a dedicated column or subsection for Business Day adjustments, specifying whether the deadline moves forward, backward, or remains unchanged if it falls on a non-Business Day. Flag missing adjustment mechanisms as critical issues.

Before finalising a timeline analysis, cross-check all date-based obligations against the governing document's Business Day definition. Verify whether deadlines adjust for weekends/holidays and flag discrepancies between computed and stated dates.

For every critical date in a timeline analysis, explicitly state: (1) the computed calendar date, (2) whether it falls on a Business Day, (3) the document's Business Day definition, and (4) whether adjustments are required or ambiguous.

When reconciling date-based obligations, use a date calculator to independently verify all deadlines. Document the arithmetic steps and cross-check against the document's stated dates to identify discrepancies or ambiguities.
